tweet.text:
I don't think this is a rationalist value - like I said, I've never debated in public before.

And I don't think Pinker is particularly standing up for academic values here. So far his main contributions to the mass discourse have been to say, or to boost other people saying, that we're only scared of AI because we're male, that we can't be trusted because we live "unconventional lifestyles", that our beliefs are inherently insensitive to people worried about near-term AI risks (while we march alongside them at protests, and he makes fun of them), that we're paranoid, that we should be laughed out of the room, and every other dirty attack he can think of.

I've already discussed this topic with him a few years ago, sort of, through a confusing many-person combination of blog posts and emails, and I thought his perspective was muddled and not up to the gravity of the situation. We discussed our models of the future, imho mine aged well while his was decisively disproven (he suggested that LLMs would never be able to do things like simple arithmetic, although his exact wording was a bit slippery, you can see bits of it at https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=6524 although you'll have to follow all the links for context), and he kept insulting us anyway.

Because he's such an important public intellectual, thousands of people take his opinions seriously. They correctly admire him for his brilliant work in linguistics and cognitive science, and assume that if such an eminent thinker is saying so, we must be weird morons who hate technology and don't understand basic reasoning. I would like to trap him in a room where I can force him to defend his object-level opinions on the facts at hand, so that people can decide how much to trust his vituperations based on his specific arguments rather than his general eminence. I think that, teased out into the light of day, his arguments will be revealed as too flimsy to justify the intensity with which he belittles us.

I offered to bet $5000 not because I think money tracks correctness, because I wanted to provide a costly signal that I care about this, plus an incentive for him to participate (and maybe a little bit because it would make the debate offer go viral). If I could have just offered him $5000 to debate me, I would have done that instead, but that would have been even weirder!
